title: fix(sse): streaming chunking/framing fixes for partial JSON, delimiter and token/event ordering
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: Several customers reported occasional malformed streaming responses when using the OpenAI-compatible SSE endpoint: partial JSON objects and out-of-order delimiter/token events when chunk boundaries split tokens or when the connection closed mid-event. This introduced downstream JSON parse errors and caused clients to discard partial results. Root cause: the framing logic in sse_emitter allowed race conditions between socket flush/close and the internal chunk-assembly buffer; tokenization assumed chunk boundaries aligned with logical events and occasionally injected delimiters in the wrong order. Fix summary: 1) canonicalize framing by introducing a small deterministic sequence header on each SSE event to enforce ordering without changing the external API (sequence-id as a monotonic integer attached to the internal event envelope only); 2) ensure delimiters (partial-json boundary markers) are emitted as dedicated SSE events and flushed before token events that complete the JSON object; 3) update the reassembly logic in redwood-openai-compat so that partial JSON tokens are reassembled by sequence-id, not by arrival order; 4) add defensive checks to drop duplicate delimiter events and log metric counters for delimiter-mismatch occurrences; 5) add unit and integration tests (fuzzed chunk splits) and a golden streaming test to prevent regressions. Checklist: - [x] Add deterministic sequence header to internal SSE envelope - [x] Emit delimiter events as first-class SSE events and flush ordering - [x] Rework reassembly to use sequence-id ordering - [x] Add metrics (sse.delimiter.mismatch, sse.sequence.reorder) - [x] Add unit/fuzz tests and stream-integration tests - [x] Update compat docs and changelog Files touched: sse/emitter.rs, sse/compat/openai_stream.rs, sse/tests/fuzz_stream_split.rs, sse/tests/golden_streaming.rs, docs/openai-compat.md, observability/metrics.yaml Additional notes: This keeps the external SSE wire format unchanged for customers (the sequence header is internal-only and not surfaced in public schema). The changes are backward-compatible for existing clients but harden against partial-chunk races and are intended to reduce incident noise for streaming consumers.
commits: a1f4d2c: canonicalize internal SSE envelope and add sequence-id header
b7c8e3d: emit delimiter events as separate SSE messages and flush before token completion
d0921aa: reassembly logic now orders by sequence-id and drops duplicates
f4b9c6e: add metrics and counters for delimiter mismatches & reorderings
c3d5f2b: add unit/fuzz tests for chunk-split scenarios and golden streaming test
e6a7b8f: docs: update openai-compat streaming notes and changelog entry
review_comments: Ethan Cole: Please add explicit ordering tests that simulate connection close mid-event — existing fuzz test looks good but add a deterministic case.
Ava Martinez: Added golden_streaming.rs deterministic close-mid-event test and updated fuzz harness to cover the scenario.
Priya Singh: Can you explain why we need a sequence-id if TCP already provides ordering? Concern is increased state in emitter.

Ava Martinez: Sequence-id is kept internal to guard against re-ordering that can occur when multiple internal threads/buffers multiplex events to the same socket and when we reassemble events in the compatibility layer — it's a lightweight monotonic integer per stream and avoids having to change consumer semantics.
Marcus Huang: LGTM pending CI flakes resolved. One nit: metrics name should follow kebab-case; updated metric names included.
Ava Martinez: Updated metrics.yaml to use kebab-case and added instrumentation in openai_stream.rs.
release_notes: Fixes a class of streaming SSE malformed-JSON/parsing errors caused by chunk boundary races. Improves reliability of OpenAI-compatible streaming endpoints. No API breaking changes.
